statement: More broadly, it is also interesting to see what happens as we allow more than one partial complementation; how quickly can we recognize the class G (k) for some class G? context: In this paper we initiated the study of Partial Complement to G. Many interesting questions remain open. In particular, what is the complexity of the problem when G is the class of chordal graphs, the class of interval graphs, the class of graph excluding a path P5 as an induced subgraph, the class graphs with max degree ≤ r, or the class of graphs with min degree ≥ r More broadly, it is also interesting to see what happens as we allow more than one partial complementation; how quickly can we recognize the class G (k) for some class G? It will also be interesting to investigate what happens if we combine partial complementation with other graph modifications, such as the Seidel switch.
